audit.whatIsWrong: Level 1 rendered as Trundle directly above whys[0] 'You own level 1 outright'; Level 6 rendered as Trundle above whys[4] 'R is a tempo and roam window'; 2+ items rendered as Quinn above whys[6] 'his drain-tank scaling reclaims the 2+ items window'. Three rows contradicted their own reasons.
audit.why: The mirror audit (trundle__quinn) already set this chart to Quinn / Skill / Quinn / Quinn / Quinn / Quinn / Trundle, and the packet agrees. I am restating the same rows from this side.
audit.corrected: Rows 0 and 4 to Quinn, row 6 to Trundle, one atomic group across both layers, with the three ratings and phases[6].why brought into line.

audit.why: Quinn levels 1-3, level 6 as a roam window rather than a duel, first-item lethality, Trundle at 2+ items when Subjugate finally outscales — matches the mirror's placement exactly. Subjugate's 120s at rank 1 is now stated, which is what makes the roam window safe.
audit.corrected: Cooldown written into phases[4].why and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three interactions absent. Subjugate steals health, armour AND magic resistance, and the stolen amount DOUBLES over 4 seconds — nothing on the page told the player that breaking away early halves it. Pillar of Ice is impassable terrain that walls off a retreat path, described only as 'pin you', which it does not do. And Chomp is an auto-attack reset, so the tell is the attack wind-up, not a cast animation.
audit.why: Riot text for R: 'Trundle immediately steals a percent of his target's Health, Armor and Magic Resistance. Over the next 4 seconds the amount stolen is doubled.' Riot text for E: 'creates an ice pillar at target location, becoming impassable terrain and slowing all nearby enemy units.' The kit file flags Chomp with autoReset, and the missing-interactions file flags the burst tell explicitly.
audit.corrected: The doubling window, the resistance component and the terrain behaviour written into breakdown.cooldowns, report[5].t, dosFull[0].d, dontsFull[1].d and wants.foe[1].

audit.whatIsWrong: report[8].t buys anti-heal, which is right, but nothing explained WHERE it matters: Frozen Domain increases his healing from all sources, so the same trade inside his zone heals far more than outside it. Separately, Plated Steelcaps is a weak answer when Subjugate is stealing armour off you and giving it to him.
audit.why: Riot text for W: 'gaining Attack Speed, Move Speed, and increased healing from all sources while on it.' The missing-interactions file also flags resistances-invalidated for King's Tribute and Subjugate.
audit.corrected: Frozen Domain's healing amplification written into dontsFull[0].d; the resistance-steal caveat into dontsFull[1].d.

notes: Following the mirror, I did NOT claim that Pillar of Ice blocks or shortens a Vault that is already in flight — the mirror flagged that as unverified and Riot's text does not settle it. The page only says the pillar is impassable terrain that closes a retreat path, which the text does support. Two consistency oddities left alone because they are enum/rating judgements the mirror should settle: diff reads 'FAV' while diffRating is 7.5/10 and report[14].t calls it 'Tricky', and the tone colour is the orange normally used for hard lanes, against a 57.43% win rate.
